newsitem.title: USA: Iraq oil deal hike not likely soon - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Iraq oil deal hike not likely soon - diplomat.

text.p: The United Nations is not likely to consider an increase in Iraq's "oil-for-food" deal until at least the end of the first 180-day period, according to a well-placed western diplomatic source at the U.N.
"There has been no formal request (from Baghdad) for an increase and at this stage one certainly wouldn't be considered," the source said.

Earlier on Friday, Iraq's oil minister, Amir Muhammad Rasheed, was quoted as saying that U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan would suggest an increase in the deal when he reports on the first 90-days at the end of next week.

The accord stipulates a monetary cap on Iraq's oil sales of $2 billion over six months, with $1 billion in each 90-day period. The deal commenced on December 10 and, though the 90-day review is due next week, no formal reconsideration of the deals terms is expected until June.

"This is Iraq's way of talking this up but I doubt that (an increase in the $2 billion limit) is even on the cards for the end of the 180-day period. The most likely scenario is a straightforward renewal," the source said.

Iraq has informally stated many times in the past that it wants an increase in the amount of the deal, "but there is no justification for that at the moment...the first goods haven't even arrived yet," the diplomat said.

Though Iraq has sold all of the oil allotted for the first 90 days and had about $600 million in the U.N.-administered escrow account at the end of last week, the shipment of humanitarian goods has followed slowly.
The first foodstuffs shipment is not expected until the middle or second half of March and medicial supplies not until April.
"Once they arrive they will be stored in central facilities until the government of Iraq decides it can be distrubuted in a fair manner," a U.N. spokesman said Friday.
"The U.N. will be fully operational to observe distrubution of food by March 15," he said, adding that observation for medical supplies dispersement is also ready.
"Even by the end of the first 180 day period they won't have full supplies for that period so it will still be premature" to consider an increase, the diplomat said.

The U.N. spokesman noted that the U.N.'s 90-day report was still being drafted and that Iraq's foreign minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf will meet in New York Friday morning with Asushi Akashi, head of the U.N.'s Humanitarian Affairs Department and chiefly responsible for the oil deal's implementation.
